Implementation plan · 20 Nov 2026 · baseline commit bf678a8

dtech-aidlc Enhancement Plan

59 tasks in 5 milestones that take dtech-aidlc from a single-intent prototype to a tool a team can run, intent after intent, on a codebase that already has its own documentation.

59tasks, one pull request each
20P0
26P1
13P2
18shared contracts

What is broken today

  • A project can run only one intent. Once it finishes, orchestrate next --intent refuses every new one.
  • Approval gates are an honour system. Every stage can be reported skipped with no approval and no artifact, and the CLI still prints approval: "approved".
  • Knowledge is written and never read. Nothing loads .aidlc/knowledge/, and there is no file where a team writes its own rules.
  • On an existing project, onboard copies only files named like a BRD. The rest of docs/ never reaches the workflow.

What this plan delivers

  • Milestone 1. The engine holds: many intents, real gates, verified artifacts, safe migration.
  • Milestone 2. The knowledge loop: PROJECT.md, registered sources, validated records, refreshable skills.
  • Milestone 3. Brownfield: existing docs registered by reference, a codebase map, regression runs.
  • Milestones 4 and 5. Installers, accurate docs, then the methodology backlog.

Status: Every task was planned, reviewed against the code, reconciled with the shared contracts and audited as a whole. The audit corrected 11 tasks and spot-checked about 60 file and line citations against bf678a8. Its mechanical fixes are applied here; the 3 points it left for a decision are listed under Known open points.

Loading plan data for the copy buttons.

Working rules for the coder

  1. Follow the milestone order, then the task order inside each milestone. Every milestone ships on its own. Nothing depends on a later milestone unless the task says which stub it uses until then.
  2. One task is one pull request. Each task lists its files, the change, acceptance criteria and the tests to add. A task is done when every acceptance criterion can be shown from the CLI or the file system.
  3. The shared contracts are authoritative. When a name, JSON shape, path or message is used by more than one task, the contract section defines it. If a task and a contract ever disagree, the contract wins and the task text is the bug.
  4. Line numbers refer to commit bf678a8. After the first tasks land, find code by the behaviour the task quotes.
  5. Keep the project's constraints. No runtime dependencies, Node 20 or newer, node:test, no network. Keep atomic writes, symlink refusal, mode 0600 for local state and non-destructive projection.
  6. Existing projects must keep working. Where state or projected files change shape, the task states the migration. Do not ship a change that needs a manual step unless the task says so.
  7. Before every pull request: npm test and npm run lint pass. The baseline is 27 passing tests.
  8. Open decisions: each workstream lists questions for the owner with a recommendation. Build on the recommendation unless the owner says otherwise.

Priorities: P0 the core promise is broken without it, P1 needed for team or brownfield use, P2 polish or backlog. Effort: S under half a day, M up to two days, L more than two days.

Design decisions the plan is built on

  • D1
    Project knowledge is a human-written PROJECT.md

    Conventions, domain rules, architecture notes and glossary live in PROJECT.md at the project root. onboard and init create it from a template only when it is absent. The tool never overwrites it.

  • D2
    Knowledge sources are registered by reference

    A committed manifest, aidlc.knowledge.json, lists PROJECT.md, docs/ and any other source by path. Files are read in place. Nothing is copied into .aidlc.

  • D3
    The knowledge house is .aidlc/knowledge/

    One record per closed intent at .aidlc/knowledge/<intent-id>.md. The CLI creates the folder, supplies a record template, keeps an index and validates the record at the knowledge-writeback gate.

  • D4
    Context travels in the orchestrate next directive

    The JSON printed by orchestrate next gains a context object that lists what the stage may read. This reaches every harness without re-projecting SKILL.md.

  • D5
    The stage graph declares inputs

    core/data/phase-graph.json gains inputs per stage, so contracts.md and the data agree about what an agent may read.

  • D6
    A project runs many intents in sequence

    Finished intents stay under .aidlc/intents/<id>/. Completion is derived from stage statuses.

  • D7
    Gates need a human, stages need their artifacts

    No gate is passed without an explicit recorded approval, whatever the reported result. A stage cannot be reported complete until the files it produces exist at a defined path.

  • D8
    The tool defines what a team commits

    onboard and init write the ignore rules. Nothing meant to be committed contains an absolute machine path.

Milestones

  1. 1

    The engine holdsrelease 0.1.3

    A user can run one intent after another in the same project. A phase gate cannot be passed, by completing or by skipping, without a recorded approval that names the approver, and a stage cannot be reported complete until every file it produces exists at the path the CLI printed. Projects started with the current version, including the old state shape that crashes today, are migrated automatically with a backup. Wrong options fail with a clear message, and doctor checks state against the graph. No file under harness/ changes, so skills already projected into projects keep working; the directive and the error messages carry the new rules.

  3. 3

    Brownfield onboardingrelease 0.3.0

    Running onboard in an existing project registers the documentation that is already there by reference, with a kind for each entry, and prints what was registered and how to correct it; nothing is copied into .aidlc. Every directive says whether the project is an existing codebase, whether registered documents changed since the last scan, and where the one-time codebase map is. Develop work is planned against existing code and the existing test suite is run and reported before the release-candidate gate. init and onboard are one command, a project can carry both harnesses, and re-running onboard is safe.

ENG-01Strict, table-driven argument parsing with clear error messagesP1M

Engine integrity · milestone 1 · effort M (up to two days)

Problem today

parseArgs (core/tools/lib.mjs:117-128) accepts every --flag and turns a flag whose value is missing, empty, or starts with '--' into the boolean true; only the repos command checks its flags (core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:170-171). As a result 'onboard --docs docs' exits 0 and ignores the option, 'orchestrate next --intent' and an intent text starting with '--' crash with 'text.toLowerCase is not a function' (:18), 'status --project' crashes inside resolve (:55), '--detail' with no value stores true (:156), '--version' alone prints the help text (:52-53), and 'deps add constructor x' / 'deps pull toString' crash on inherited object properties (:194, :198). In addition the help text is one source line of 1,571 characters (dtech-aidlc.mjs:11) that at least fourteen later tasks in four workstreams must edit, and the repository has no release-notes file although many tasks change behaviour that users must be told about.

Depends on

  • Nothing. This task can start first.

Files

  • core/tools/lib.mjs:117-128 (rewrite parseArgs)
  • core/tools/cli-spec.mjs (new)
  • core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:11 (HELP becomes an array), :50-55 (parsing, command key, --help, --version, --project), :57-58, :133-135, :151-156 (option reads), :168-173 (remove the repos-only allow-list), :189-198 (deps lookups)
  • tests/helpers.mjs (new)

Change

(1)Rewrite parseArgs(argv, optionTypes) in lib.mjs. optionTypes maps an option name to 'string', 'boolean' or 'list'. Rules: a bare '--' ends option parsing and everything after it is positional. '--name=value' and '--name value' are both accepted. For 'string' and 'list' the value is the inline part or the next token taken verbatim even when it starts with '--'; but when the value is missing, is the empty string, is exactly '--', or is itself a known option (exactly '--known' or starting with '--known=' for a name in optionTypes), throw Option --name requires a non-empty value. A 'boolean' option never consumes the next token; written with '=value' it throws Option --name does not take a value. A 'string' option given twice throws Option --name was given more than once. A 'list' option collects every occurrence into an array (no ENG command uses 'list'; it exists from this task on so that BRN can register the repeatable --docs). A name that is not in optionTypes is pushed to an 'unknown' array and does not consume the next token. Return { positional, flags, unknown }, with flags created by Object.create(null).
(2)Create core/tools/cli-spec.mjs. It is the only option validator of the product: every workstream registers its commands and options in it and writes no option check of its own. It must have no side effects and import nothing from dtech-aidlc.mjs, because dtech-aidlc.mjs runs main() when imported (:203) and tests need to import the table. Exports: GLOBAL_FLAGS = { project: 'string', help: 'boolean', version: 'boolean' }; TWO_WORD_COMMANDS = ['orchestrate', 'config', 'repos', 'deps', 'completion', 'intent', 'knowledge', 'harness'] (the last three have no rows yet; ENG-03, KNW-01 and HRN-03 add them, and listing the words now means no later task touches the key rule); COMMAND_FLAGS, an object keyed by command key whose values map option name to type, with exactly today's options: 'init' and 'onboard': { harness: 'string', scope: 'string' }; 'orchestrate next': { intent: 'string', description: 'string', scope: 'string' }; 'orchestrate report': { result: 'string', approval: 'string', detail: 'string', stage: 'string' }; 'repos add': { ref: 'string' }; 'repos pull': { file: 'string' }; and empty objects for 'scope', 'status', 'doctor', 'config agents', 'repos list', 'repos remove', 'deps add', 'deps list', 'deps pull', 'completion zsh'; COMMAND_MAX_ARGS, the largest number of positional arguments after the command words: 0 for init, onboard, status, doctor, 'orchestrate next', 'orchestrate report', 'repos list', 'deps list', 'completion zsh'; 1 for scope, 'repos pull', 'repos remove', 'deps pull'; 2 for 'repos add' and 'deps add'; 3 for 'config agents'; commandKey(positionals), which returns the first positional, or the first two joined by a space when the first is in TWO_WORD_COMMANDS and a second exists; and optionTypes(), which merges GLOBAL_FLAGS and every COMMAND_FLAGS entry and throws if one option name has two different types. The words 'help' and 'version' are handled before the table is consulted and have no row.
(3)main() flow in dtech-aidlc.mjs: parse with optionTypes(); if flags.help is set or the first positional is 'help', print the help text; if flags.version is set or the first positional is 'version', print the single line dtech-aidlc <version> (this check must come before the command defaults to help); otherwise build the key with commandKey. Then, before any file-system access: if 'unknown' is not empty, or a parsed option is neither global nor listed for the key, throw Unknown option --docs for 'onboard'. Allowed options: --harness, --scope, --project. (report the first offending option; the allowed list is the row's options followed by --project; when the key is not in COMMAND_FLAGS only the global options are allowed and the text is Unknown option --x. Run 'dtech-aidlc help'.); if the number of remaining positionals exceeds COMMAND_MAX_ARGS, throw Unexpected argument 'extra' for 'status' naming the first surplus argument. A key that is not in the table and has no bad option falls through to today's errors ('Unknown command ...; use dtech-aidlc help', 'Use orchestrate next or orchestrate report', and so on). Existing 'too few arguments' usage errors stay as they are. Remove the special allow-list at :170-171.
(4)In the deps branch use Object.hasOwn(state.dependencies, id) for every lookup, create a missing entry by explicit assignment, and use Object.hasOwn(state.stages, id) for the status lookup at :198.
(5)Help text. Rewrite HELP (:11) as an array of strings joined with a newline, one command or sentence per source line, so that later tasks add a line without touching a neighbour's line. The printed text stays byte-identical to today's except for these additions: the 'orchestrate next' line becomes 'orchestrate next [--intent TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--scope NAME]'; the 'orchestrate report' line gains '[--detail TEXT] [--stage ID]'; the 'repos pull' line gains '[--file FILE]'; and one new line after the command list reads exactly 'Global option: --project DIR Use DIR as the project root instead of the current directory.'
(6)Create tests/helpers.mjs exporting: repo (repository root), cli (path of dtech-aidlc.mjs), tempProject(t, prefix) (temporary directory removed after the test), run(project, ...args) (spawns the CLI with '--project <project>' appended and cwd set to the project), runRaw(cwd, ...args) (spawns the CLI with exactly the given arguments), json(project, ...args) (asserts exit 0 and parses stdout), runWithStdin(project, text, ...args) (like run, with the text as standard input), and initProject(project, scope = 'solo', harness = 'claude') (runs 'init --harness <harness> --scope <scope>' and asserts exit 0). It is a single file; no tests/helpers folder is created. Later tasks add readActiveState (ENG-02), completeStage and driveToCompletion (ENG-03), writeArtifacts (ENG-09), and helpText and helpCommands (HRN-08).
(7)Create CHANGELOG.md at the repository root: a title '# Changelog', one sentence saying that each release lists the behaviour changes a user or a script can notice, and a section '## 0.1.3' with two entries: unknown options, options without a value and unexpected extra arguments now make a command fail before anything is written, and the message lists the allowed options; 'dtech-aidlc --version' prints only the version line. ENG-10, the last task of milestone 1, completes this section; the last task of each later milestone adds that milestone's section. The file is not installed (scripts/install.sh copies only core/, harness/ and package.json).

Acceptance criteria

  • In an empty directory D, 'dtech-aidlc onboard --bogus x --project D' exits 1, stderr contains Unknown option --bogus for 'onboard' and Allowed options: --harness, --scope, --project, and D/.aidlc does not exist ('--docs' behaves the same until BRN-03 registers it).
  • 'dtech-aidlc orchestrate next --intent' and 'dtech-aidlc orchestrate next --intent ""' exit 1 with stderr dtech-aidlc: Option --intent requires a non-empty value; the word 'toLowerCase' does not appear.
  • 'dtech-aidlc orchestrate next --intent --project D' exits 1 with the same 'requires a non-empty value' message.
  • In an initialized project, 'dtech-aidlc orchestrate next --intent "--fix the login bug"' exits 0 and the printed directive has intent '--fix the login bug' and intentId 'fix-the-login-bug'.
  • 'dtech-aidlc status --project' exits 1 with Option --project requires a non-empty value.
  • With an active stage, 'orchestrate report --result skipped --detail' and 'orchestrate report --result complete --detial x' both exit 1 and no file under .aidlc changes (compare the bytes of every file before and after).
  • 'dtech-aidlc --version' prints exactly one line 'dtech-aidlc <version from package.json>'.
  • With an active intent, 'deps add constructor x' exits 0 and prints an object with id 'constructor' and dependencies ['x']; 'deps pull toString' exits 0 and prints id 'toString' with an empty dependencies array.
  • 'dtech-aidlc status extra' exits 1 with Unexpected argument 'extra' for 'status'.
  • 'dtech-aidlc --help' contains the line 'Global option: --project DIR Use DIR as the project root instead of the current directory.' and the strings '--description TEXT', '--detail TEXT', '--stage ID' and '--file FILE'; every line that the command prints at commit bf678a8, other than the three changed command lines, is still printed.
  • awk 'length($0) > 400' core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs prints nothing (the help text is no longer one long line).
  • node -e "import('./core/tools/cli-spec.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.commandKey(['knowledge','sources','add'])))" prints 'knowledge sources' and nothing else; commandKey(['status','x']) returns 'status'.
  • CHANGELOG.md exists at the repository root and contains the heading '## 0.1.3'.
  • 'npm test' passes (27 existing tests plus the new ones).

Tests

  • tests/args.test.mjs (new): unit tests that import parseArgs from core/tools/lib.mjs and cover inline and separate values, a value starting with '--', a missing value, an empty value, a value that is a known option, a duplicate string option, a list option given twice, a boolean followed by a positional (the positional is not consumed), a boolean with '=value', an unknown option, and the '--' terminator.
  • tests/args.test.mjs: CLI tests for every acceptance line above, using tests/helpers.mjs (runRaw for the '--project' with no value case; initProject before every 'orchestrate next').
  • tests/args.test.mjs: a test that imports COMMAND_FLAGS, TWO_WORD_COMMANDS and commandKey from core/tools/cli-spec.mjs and checks, for every key, that the command with '--bogus' appended exits 1 and creates no .aidlc directory, that optionTypes() does not throw, and that commandKey returns two words exactly for the eight listed first words.
  • Existing tests/repos-cli.test.mjs:61 ('repos pull --bogus' exits 1) keeps passing unchanged; no other existing test passes an unknown option, a duplicated option or a value-less option (checked against all seven test files).

Risks

Scripts or agents that passed options which were silently ignored now fail; that is the intended change, the message lists the allowed options, and CHANGELOG.md says so. Because a string option takes the next token verbatim, 'orchestrate next --intent --draft' treats '--draft' as the intent text; this is accepted so that real intent texts starting with '--' work. Other workstreams add rows to core/tools/cli-spec.mjs, lines to the HELP array and lines to core/tools/completion.zsh; merge conflicts in those three places are likely and trivial. HRN-08 (directly after this task) adds the test that keeps the three in step and adds the 'onboard' entry to completion.zsh; this task does not touch completion.zsh.

ENG-02State version 2: pointer file plus one state file per intent, atomic and symlink-safe writes, automatic migration, loud failure on corrupt stateP0L

Engine integrity · milestone 1 · effort L (more than two days)

Problem today

The root .aidlc/state.json is read with a helper that swallows every error (core/tools/lib.mjs:26, :100), so a truncated file is treated as 'no intent' and silently replaced by the next --intent (core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:32, :38-46). State is written non-atomically to the root file and to a mirror (lib.mjs:101; dtech-aidlc.mjs:22-30), and the mirror goes stale after 'deps add' (:195). The version field is never checked: a state without intentId (the shape of this repository's own .aidlc/state.json) makes 'orchestrate next' write state and audit (:139-140) and then crash at :144, after which 'orchestrate report' advances the pointer blind. 'init' (:68-74), 'orchestrate report' (:146-158), 'deps add' (:195) and audit() (lib.mjs:102-107) write through a symlinked .aidlc, while 'orchestrate next' and 'config' refuse it (agent-models.mjs:10). The absolute project path is written into state (:42), intent.md (:45) and the first audit row (:74). There is no shared atomic-write or symlink-check helper, so each workstream was about to write its own with a different error message.

Depends on

  • ENG-01

Files

  • core/tools/workflow.mjs (new)
  • core/tools/lib.mjs:99-107 (loadState, saveState, audit; add writeFileAtomic, writeJsonAtomic, readJsonStrict, assertNoSymlinkComponents, assertSafeStateDir)
  • core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:16-49 (helpers move to workflow.mjs), :55 (safety check), :74 (audit row), :111-114 (status), :124-125 (doctor's state check), :130-160 (orchestrate), :188-199 (deps)
  • tests/state-migration.test.mjs (new)
  • tests/cli-integration.test.mjs:113-120, :141-142
  • tests/helpers.mjs (add readActiveState)

Change

(1)In core/tools/lib.mjs add the shared safe-write and safe-path helpers. They are the only ones in the product: HRN-01, HRN-02, KNW-01 and BRN-02 reuse them and add no writer or symbolic-link check of their own. writeFileAtomic(path, text, { mode = 0o600 } = {}): throws Refusing to write through symlink: <path> when lstat shows that the target exists and is a symbolic link; otherwise writes the text to '<path>.<pid>.<random>.tmp' with flag 'wx' and the given mode, renames it over the target, and removes the temporary file when any step fails (the pattern of agent-models.mjs:39-45). It does not create missing parent directories; the caller does. writeJsonAtomic(path, value): calls writeFileAtomic with JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) plus a final newline and mode 0o600; a caller that needs another mode (KNW and HRN use 0o644 for committed files at the project root and in .aidlc/knowledge) calls writeFileAtomic with the JSON text. readJsonStrict(path): returns undefined when the file is absent and throws <path> cannot be parsed as JSON when it does not parse. assertNoSymlinkComponents(root, relativePath): walks the components of relativePath below root (root itself is not checked), calls lstat on each one that exists, and throws Refusing to write through symlink: <path of that component relative to root, with forward slashes> for the first symbolic link; it stops at the first component that does not exist. assertSafeStateDir(root): throws Refusing to access symlink .aidlc directory when .aidlc exists and is a symbolic link (same wording as core/tools/agent-models.mjs:10), Refusing unsafe .aidlc path when it exists and is not a directory (same wording as core/tools/dependencies.mjs:59), then calls assertNoSymlinkComponents(root, '.aidlc/intents') and throws Refusing unsafe .aidlc/intents path when that path exists and is not a directory. Message rule for every workstream: a symbolic link at .aidlc itself is always reported by assertSafeStateDir as 'Refusing to access symlink .aidlc directory'; a link deeper in the tree is reported as 'Refusing to write through symlink: <path>'. Make audit() (lib.mjs:102-107) call assertSafeStateDir and refuse a symlinked audit.jsonl with 'Refusing to write through symlink: .aidlc/audit.jsonl'. In main(), call assertSafeStateDir(root) right after the project root is resolved (dtech-aidlc.mjs:55) for every command except help, version and completion. Delete loadState and saveState once no caller remains.
(2)Create core/tools/workflow.mjs (no side effects on import). It is the only module that reads or writes a state.json. Exports: intentDir(root, id); intentStatePath(root, id); readPointer(root), returning { kind: 'absent' }, { kind: 'pointer', activeIntentId }, { kind: 'legacy', state } or { kind: 'corrupt', reason }; loadWorkflow(root, graph, { migrate = false } = {}), returning { activeIntentId, state, legacy } where state is the validated state of the active intent or null; loadIntent(root, graph, id); saveIntent(root, state) (sets updatedAt, creates the intent folder when absent, calls assertNoSymlinkComponents(root, '.aidlc/intents/<id>/state.json') and writes with writeJsonAtomic); savePointer(root, activeIntentId) (writes exactly { version: 2, activeIntentId, updatedAt } with writeJsonAtomic); validateIntentState(state, graph, folderId), returning an array of problem strings. The root file is a pointer when it is an object with version 2 and an activeIntentId that is null or matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$; other keys are ignored on load and dropped on the next write. The file .aidlc/intents/<id>/state.json is the only copy of an intent's state, has version 2, no 'project' key and no absolute path. New intent.md files contain '# <intentId>', a blank line and the intent text, with no 'Project:' line; existing intent.md files are left as they are (KNW-09 cleans files written by older versions).
(3)Loading rules. Root file absent: no active intent. Root file not parseable: throw .aidlc/state.json cannot be parsed. No changes were made. Intents on disk: <ids, comma separated, or 'none'>. Run 'dtech-aidlc doctor' for details. Root file parseable but neither a pointer nor an object with a 'stages' object: throw the same text with 'is not a recognised state file' in place of 'cannot be parsed'. Root file with a 'stages' object: version 1, handled as in (4). Pointer naming an intent whose state file is absent: throw Active intent '<id>' has no state file at .aidlc/intents/<id>/state.json. No changes were made. Per-intent file unparseable or invalid: throw <relative path> is invalid: <first problem>. No changes were made. The problems validateIntentState reports are: not an object; 'intent' not a non-empty string; 'scope' not a key of graph.scopes; 'stages' not an object; a stage row that is not an object or whose status is not in_progress, complete, blocked or skipped; 'intentId' not matching the id pattern or different from the folder name; 'currentStage' neither null nor a stage of the scope; 'dependencies' present and not an object of string arrays. Every field except version, intentId, intent, scope and stages is optional on load. Stage keys unknown to the graph are tolerated. Normalisation applied in memory on every load: drop 'project', set version 2, default 'dependencies' to {}, replace a stage row 'detail' that is not a string by null (the old CLI could store true), and recompute nothing else in this task. A per-intent file with version 1 (a mirror left by the old CLI) is accepted.
(4)Migration, done only when loadWorkflow is called with migrate true, which the writing commands do (orchestrate next, orchestrate report, deps add, and the intent commands of ENG-03) before anything else. First normalise and validate the old root content (with its own intentId, or without the id checks when it has none); when it is invalid throw .aidlc/state.json is invalid: <problem>. No changes were made. Case a, old root with intentId: the root content is authoritative (it holds 'deps add' edits that the mirror lacks); write it, normalised, to intents/<intentId>/state.json, creating the folder and intent.md when absent. Case b, old root without intentId: compute the id with the existing intentSlug function and uniqueness loop (dtech-aidlc.mjs:39-41), but reuse an existing intents/<slug>/ folder whose state.json has the same 'intent' and 'createdAt' (this makes a re-run after an interrupted migration idempotent); create the folder and intent.md when absent; write the state with the new intentId. Then for both cases, in this order: copy the original root file byte for byte to .aidlc/state.v1.bak.json with flag 'wx' and mode 0o600 (skip when it already exists; the copy keeps the old 'project' value, which KNW-09 reads later); replace the root with the pointer using savePointer; append the audit row state.migrated { from: 1, intentId }. With migrate false (status, doctor, deps list, deps pull) the old root is normalised and validated in memory and returned as { activeIntentId: <its intentId or null>, state, legacy: true }; nothing is written and no id is invented. 'status' then prints what it prints today for that state plus "migration": "pending".
(5)Rewire status, orchestrate next, orchestrate report and deps to these functions and delete ensureState and persistWorkflow, without changing lifecycle behaviour yet (a different --intent text is still refused with today's message, and status 'complete' is still set by the extra 'orchestrate next'; ENG-03 changes both). 'deps add' saves the per-intent state. 'orchestrate next' must compute everything it prints before its first write. Change doctor's check at :124-125 to call readPointer and report kind 'corrupt' as a failed 'State JSON is readable' check.
(6)Write the 'projection' field of the project.initialized audit row (:74) relative to the project root, with '/' separators, so that no audit row contains an absolute path.

Acceptance criteria

  • Fresh project: after 'init --harness claude --scope solo' and 'orchestrate next --intent "Add CSV export"', .aidlc/state.json parses to an object whose keys are exactly activeIntentId, updatedAt and version, with version 2 and activeIntentId 'add-csv-export'; .aidlc/intents/add-csv-export/state.json has version 2 and no 'project' key; intent.md has no line starting 'Project:'; 'grep -r <absolute project path> .aidlc/intents .aidlc/audit.jsonl' prints nothing.

'orchestrate next' exits 0 and prints a directive with intentId 'test' and stage.id 'problem-framing'. Afterwards the root file is a pointer to 'test', .aidlc/intents/test/state.json and intent.md exist, .aidlc/state.v1.bak.json is byte-identical to the original file, and audit.jsonl contains exactly one state.migrated row. Running 'orchestrate next' again does not create .aidlc/intents/test-2.
  • Interrupted migration: the legacy fixture plus a pre-existing .aidlc/intents/test/state.json with the same intent and createdAt; 'orchestrate next' exits 0 with intentId 'test' and no folder 'test-2' exists.
  • Old-format fixture with intentId whose mirror lacks a dependency edge that the root has: after 'orchestrate next', .aidlc/intents/<id>/state.json contains the edge.
  • Truncated .aidlc/state.json: 'status' and 'orchestrate next --intent Other' both exit 1, stderr contains 'cannot be parsed' and 'No changes were made', the file bytes are unchanged, and no new folder appears under .aidlc/intents.
  • A root file containing {"hello":1}: 'orchestrate next --intent Other' exits 1 with 'is not a recognised state file'.
  • An old-format root with "scope": "galaxy": 'orchestrate next' exits 1 with 'is invalid', and neither a backup file nor an intents folder is created. A per-intent state.json edited to "scope": "galaxy": 'orchestrate next' exits 1, stderr names the file and the word scope, and no file changes.
  • With .aidlc being a symbolic link to another directory, 'init --harness claude --scope solo' exits 1 with 'Refusing to access symlink .aidlc directory' and the link target stays empty. With .aidlc a real directory and .aidlc/intents a symbolic link, 'status' exits 1 with 'Refusing to write through symlink: .aidlc/intents'.
  • Unit: writeFileAtomic on a path that is a symbolic link throws 'Refusing to write through symlink:' and leaves the link target unchanged; assertNoSymlinkComponents(root, 'a/b/c.txt') throws naming 'a/b' when a/b is a symbolic link and returns when a/b does not exist.

Tests

  • tests/state-migration.test.mjs (new): one test per acceptance line 2 to 12 (legacy migration and its idempotency, interrupted migration, old format with stale mirror, corrupt pointer, unrecognised root, invalid legacy and invalid per-intent state, symlinked .aidlc for init and symlinked .aidlc/intents, the unit tests of writeFileAtomic and assertNoSymlinkComponents imported from core/tools/lib.mjs, no temporary files and file modes (skip the mode assertion on win32), read-only status on legacy state, deps add). Risks

A migration bug could lose progress; mitigated by validating before migrating, by the byte-identical backup, by writing the per-intent file before replacing the root, and by the idempotency rule. The migration must be tried against this repository's own .aidlc/state.json shape before release. After migration the old CLI no longer works on that checkout (it refuses with 'Active intent uses scope undefined', checked in a fixture) until .aidlc/state.v1.bak.json is copied back over .aidlc/state.json; ENG-10 writes this into the 0.1.3 section of CHANGELOG.md. ENG-03Multi-intent lifecycle: start a new intent after the previous one, list, show, pause, resume and abandon intentsP0M

Engine integrity · milestone 1 · effort M (up to two days)

Problem today

ensureState refuses any --intent whose text differs from the stored one, whatever the stored intent's status, and even when the only difference is a trailing space (core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:33-34), so a project can hold one intent for its whole life. Completion is only recorded when an extra 'orchestrate next' is run after the last report (:138). There is no command to list, inspect, pause or abandon an intent (HELP at :11), and the error text 'complete or otherwise resolve it' names an action that does not help. The uniqueness loop for a new id (:39-41) looks only at .aidlc/intents, so a knowledge record that a person placed at .aidlc/knowledge/<id>.md could later be overwritten by an intent that receives the same id.

Depends on

  • ENG-02
  • HRN-08: tests/completion.test.mjs, the guard test that keeps the help text, core/tools/completion.zsh and core/tools/cli-spec.mjs in step; it must be merged first because this task adds the first new command

Files

  • core/tools/workflow.mjs (lifecycle functions, listIntents, the id uniqueness helper)
  • core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:11 (HELP array), :31-49 (ensureState logic, in workflow.mjs after ENG-02), :111-114 (status), :133-138 (next), new 'intent' command branch after :162
  • core/tools/cli-spec.mjs (new command rows)
  • core/tools/completion.zsh:28-40 (command list), :43-97 (add an 'intent' case and '--intent' for status)
  • tests/intent-lifecycle.test.mjs (new)
  • tests/helpers.mjs (add completeStage, driveToCompletion)

Change

(1)Derived status. Add deriveStatus(state, graph) to workflow.mjs: 'abandoned' when state.closed?.kind is 'abandoned'; 'complete' when every stage returned by orderedStages(graph, state.scope) has status complete or skipped; otherwise 'active'. loadIntent and saveIntent overwrite state.status with this value, so the final 'orchestrate report' already leaves the intent complete. An intent is 'finished' when its derived status is complete or abandoned.
(2)'orchestrate next' decision table, where A is the intent the pointer names (a pointer that names an abandoned intent counts as no A) and 'same text' means equal after trimming and collapsing every run of whitespace to one space. Without --intent: no A -> exit 1 No active intent. Start one with: dtech-aidlc orchestrate next --intent "...", followed, when unfinished intents exist on disk, by Paused intents: <ids>. Continue one with: dtech-aidlc intent resume <id>.; A complete -> print { complete: true, intent, intentId } and write nothing; A unfinished -> select its next stage. With --intent T: no A -> create a new intent; A complete and T is the same text -> print the complete result plus "hint": "This intent is already complete. Use a different --intent text to start new work." and start nothing (HRN-10 teaches the conductor to tell the user and not to retry); A complete and T differs -> create a new intent and move the pointer (A's folder is not touched); A unfinished and same text -> continue A; A unfinished and T differs -> exit 1 Intent '<id>' is still in progress (stage <current stage, or the next unfinished stage>, <done> of <total> stages finished). Finish it, set it aside with 'dtech-aidlc intent pause', or close it with 'dtech-aidlc intent abandon --detail "<reason>"', then start the new intent.
(3)Id uniqueness. Move the uniqueness loop into one helper in workflow.mjs, freeIntentId(root, base), used for a new intent and for migration case b of ENG-02: an id is taken when the folder .aidlc/intents/<id> exists or the file .aidlc/knowledge/<id>.md exists (checked with lstatSync on a plain path join, so a dangling symbolic link also counts; knowledge.mjs is not imported); the helper tries base, base-2, base-3 and so on. The idempotency rule of ENG-02 (reuse a folder with the same 'intent' and 'createdAt') is checked before the helper is called.
(4)New command 'intent'. Add to cli-spec.mjs: COMMAND_FLAGS 'intent list': {}, 'intent pause': { detail: 'string' }, 'intent resume': {}, 'intent abandon': { detail: 'string' }, and intent: 'string' on 'status'; COMMAND_MAX_ARGS 0 for 'intent list' and 'intent pause', 1 for 'intent resume' and 'intent abandon' ('intent' is already in TWO_WORD_COMMANDS). Every intent command calls loadWorkflow with migrate true. Export listIntents(root, graph) from workflow.mjs. It is read-only and never throws for a damaged file: it returns an array sorted by createdAt of { intentId, title (first line of the intent text, at most 80 characters), scope, status, current (true for the pointer's intent), currentStage, progress: { done, total }, createdAt, updatedAt }, where status is 'active' (unfinished and current), 'paused' (unfinished and not current), 'complete' or 'abandoned'; it reads every directory under .aidlc/intents whose name matches the id pattern; a folder whose state cannot be loaded is returned as { intentId, status: 'unreadable', error }; when the root file is an unmigrated version-1 state, that state is returned as one row with current true (replacing the row of a mirror folder with the same id); when the pointer is corrupt every row has current false. 'intent list' prints exactly the rows of listIntents and exits 0. Other workstreams call listIntents instead of opening state files: the 'knowledge check' command and the 'Knowledge:' doctor function pass the ids of the rows with status 'complete' to KNW-03's checkKnowledge. 'status --intent <id>' prints the same object as 'status' for that intent, or exits 1 with Unknown intent '<id>'. Run 'dtech-aidlc intent list'. 'status' with no active intent keeps printing { initialized, activeIntent: null } and adds pausedIntents: [ids] only when at least one unfinished intent exists on disk. 'intent pause [--detail TEXT]' requires an unfinished active intent (otherwise No unfinished active intent to pause), sets the pointer to null, leaves the intent state unchanged, appends audit row intent.paused { intentId, detail } and prints { paused: true, intentId, resumeWith: 'dtech-aidlc intent resume <id>' }. 'intent resume <id>' requires exactly one argument (Usage: intent resume <id>), that <id> exists (Unknown intent ... as above) and is not finished (Intent '<id>' is complete and cannot be resumed / Intent '<id>' was abandoned and cannot be resumed), fails with Intent '<other>' is active; pause or finish it first when the pointer names a different unfinished intent, otherwise sets the pointer, appends intent.resumed { intentId, detail: null } and prints { resumed: true, intentId, currentStage }. When readPointer returns kind 'corrupt', 'intent resume' first renames the root file to .aidlc/state.json.corrupt-<UTC time as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ> and then writes a fresh pointer; this is the only command that proceeds on a corrupt pointer. 'intent abandon [<id>] --detail TEXT' defaults to the active intent (No active intent; name the intent to abandon when there is none), requires --detail (intent abandon requires --detail "<reason>"), refuses a finished intent (Intent '<id>' is already complete / ... already abandoned), sets closed = { kind: 'abandoned', at, detail } and currentStage = null on the intent, clears the pointer when it named that intent, appends intent.abandoned { intentId, detail } and prints { abandoned: true, intentId }. When the pointer names an intent whose state file is missing, extend the ENG-02 message with Run 'dtech-aidlc intent list', then 'dtech-aidlc intent resume <id>' or 'dtech-aidlc intent pause'., and 'intent pause' and 'intent resume' are allowed to replace such a pointer.
(5)Extend the corrupt-pointer message from ENG-02 with To point the project at one of them run 'dtech-aidlc intent resume <id>'.
(6)Help and completion: add one entry per intent command to the HELP array and change the status line to 'status [--intent ID]'. The entry for 'intent list' reads 'intent list List every intent with its status; paused means: not the active intent of this checkout'. Add 'intent' to the command list of completion.zsh, an 'intent' case with the actions list, pause, resume and abandon and the option --detail, and --intent for status. tests/completion.test.mjs (HRN-08) must pass.
(7)tests/helpers.mjs: add completeStage(project, extraReportArgs = []) (runs 'orchestrate next', reports '--result complete', and when stderr says 'requires explicit --approval approved' reports again with '--approval approved'; returns the directive) and driveToCompletion(project) (repeats completeStage until 'orchestrate next' prints complete; returns the list of visited stage ids). All tests added from this task on, in every workstream, complete stages only through these helpers, so that ENG-09, KNW-06 and BRN-11 can change what a stage's files must contain in one place.

Acceptance criteria

  • After the last stage of a solo intent is reported (no extra 'orchestrate next'), 'status' prints "status": "complete".
  • Then 'orchestrate next --intent "Second task"' exits 0 with intentId 'second-task' and stage.id 'problem-framing'; the first intent's state.json is byte-identical to before; the pointer names 'second-task'.
  • While 'second-task' is unfinished, 'orchestrate next --intent "Third task"' exits 1 and stderr contains 'second-task', 'intent pause' and 'intent abandon'; 'orchestrate next --intent "Second task "' (extra spaces) exits 0 and continues the same intent.
  • 'intent list' prints two rows: the first with status 'complete', the second with status 'active' and current true. Importing listIntents from core/tools/workflow.mjs and calling it for the same project returns the same two rows and changes no file.
  • In an initialized project with a file .aidlc/knowledge/add-csv-export.md present and no intents, 'orchestrate next --intent "Add CSV export"' prints intentId 'add-csv-export-2', and the file .aidlc/knowledge/add-csv-export.md is byte-identical afterwards.
  • In an initialized project, 'intent pause' exits 0; 'status' then prints { initialized: true, activeIntent: null, pausedIntents: ['second-task'] }; 'intent list' shows 'second-task' with status 'paused'; 'orchestrate next' exits 1 with 'No active intent' and 'intent resume'; 'intent resume second-task' exits 0 and the next 'orchestrate next' selects the same stage as before the pause.
  • With intent X active and unfinished, 'intent resume <another unfinished id>' exits 1 naming X.
  • 'intent abandon' without --detail exits 1; 'intent abandon --detail "superseded"' exits 0, 'intent list' shows status 'abandoned', the pointer's activeIntentId is null, audit.jsonl has an intent.abandoned row containing 'superseded', 'intent resume <id>' exits 1 with 'was abandoned', and 'intent abandon <id> --detail x' exits 1 with 'already abandoned'.
  • 'status --intent <first id>' prints the completed intent's stages; 'status --intent nope' exits 1 with Unknown intent 'nope'.
  • Re-sending the completed intent's own text prints complete: true with a hint and creates no new folder under .aidlc/intents.
  • With .aidlc/state.json replaced by the text '{broken', 'intent resume <id>' exits 0, a file .aidlc/state.json.corrupt-* holding '{broken' exists, and 'status' works again.
  • 'dtech-aidlc help' contains 'intent list' and the sentence 'paused means: not the active intent of this checkout'; 'node --test tests/completion.test.mjs' passes, and fails when the 'intent' line is removed from core/tools/completion.zsh.

Tests

  • tests/intent-lifecycle.test.mjs (new): two consecutive intents; completion visible straight after the final report; refusal of a different text mid-intent with the new message; same text with extra whitespace continues; intent list rows and statuses, and listIntents imported directly returning the same rows without writing; the knowledge-record rule (with .aidlc/knowledge/add-csv-export.md present, 'orchestrate next --intent "Add CSV export"' prints intentId 'add-csv-export-2'); pause, status, resume round trip; resume refused while another intent is active; abandon with and without --detail, the audit row, and abandon of a finished intent; status --intent for a past and an unknown intent; repeat of a completed intent's text; pointer repair through intent resume; pointer naming a missing intent folder. Every test calls initProject first.
  • Existing tests keep passing unchanged: tests/cli-integration.test.mjs:151-153 (final 'orchestrate next' prints complete: true) and :202 (status of a fresh project is exactly { initialized: true, activeIntent: null }).

Risks

Only one intent is active per checkout; working on two at once means pause and resume. Abandon is final by design. Because per-intent state is committed, an intent a teammate is working on appears as 'paused' on another machine; the help line explains the word. An agent that resends a reworded request while an intent is in progress still gets a refusal, now with the ways out. A completed intent's exact text cannot be reused to start new work; the hint says so and HRN-10 tells the conductor to ask the user how the new work differs. HRN-10 and HRN-16 describe the intent commands in both SKILL.md files and README.md; nothing here waits for that.

ENG-05Directive builder: build before writing, correct gate fields, and the context hook for KNWP0M

Engine integrity · milestone 1 · effort M (up to two days)

Problem today

'orchestrate next' saves state and appends an audit row (core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:139-140) before it assembles the directive (:141-144), so any failure in between leaves state changed with nothing printed. The directive sets approvalRequiredAfter to the current stage id on every stage (:144), carries no gate id and no flag saying whether the stage is the phase gate, has no place for sentences the conductor must show the user, and has no place where the knowledge context of decision D4 can be attached.

Depends on

  • ENG-03

Files

  • core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:130-145 (the 'orchestrate next' branch becomes a call to orchestrateNext plus three marked positions for other workstreams), :154 (gate computation)
  • core/tools/workflow.mjs (orchestrateNext, buildDirective, gateInfo)
  • core/tools/context.mjs (new)
  • tests/directive.test.mjs (new)

Change

(1)In workflow.mjs export orchestrateNext(root, options, hooks = {}) and a pure function buildDirective(input). options is { intent: string or null, scope: string or null }. hooks is { contextProvider }, defaulting to buildDirectiveContext from context.mjs; it exists so tests can inject a provider. orchestrateNext is synchronous and runs in this order: read the graph and the validated config (validateModelConfig, as today at :134); load and migrate state; decide which intent and stage (ENG-03 rules), computing a new intent's id and state object in memory only; build the complete directive, including the context; then write (for a new intent: the folder, intent.md, the intent state and the pointer; otherwise the intent state); then append the audit rows (intent.created, stage.selected); then return the directive as a plain object. buildDirective performs no writes and is the only place where a directive key is added by any workstream (KNW-04 sets stage.inputs there, HRN-09 adds contractsFile there).
(2)Dispatch in main(). The 'orchestrate next' branch becomes: read the options; directive = orchestrateNext(root, options); print the directive. Leave three comments that mark where other workstreams add their dispatch blocks, in this fixed order: before the call, 'KNW-05: knowledgePreflight(root), read-only, may throw'; after the call and only when the directive has a stage, 'KNW-05, KNW-09: ensureKnowledgeDir, ensureIgnoreFile, stripMachinePaths, writeIndex'; after that and only when the directive has a stage, 'HRN-24: push projectionNotices(root, VERSION) onto directive.warnings'. main() may therefore change the returned object before printing it; workflow.mjs does not import projection.mjs or knowledge.mjs.
(3)Gate helpers in workflow.mjs: gateInfo(graph, scope, stage) returns { id: <the 'gate' value of the stage's phase in the graph>, phase, finalStage: <id of the last stage of that phase among orderedStages(graph, scope)> }, and a stage is a gate stage when stage.id === finalStage. Use these helpers in 'orchestrate report' as well, replacing the inline computation at dtech-aidlc.mjs:154. Gate ids are always read from the graph.
(4)Directive fields added: stage.phaseGate (boolean); gate: { id, phase, finalStage }; approvalRequiredAfter now equals gate.finalStage; warnings: [] (a top-level array of plain sentences, always present on a stage directive; it is the channel for sentences about project setup and tool state: ENG-06 pushes the scope and configuration sentences and HRN-24 the projection state; sentences about knowledge sources and documents go to context.warnings, which KNW owns; there is no key named 'notices'); context (present only when the provider returns a value other than null or undefined). The 'stage' object is still built by spreading the graph's stage entry. All existing keys (intent, intentId, intentDir, scope, and stage.id, phase, order, agent, produces, phaseFile, agentFile, model, modelSource) keep their names and values. The result for a finished intent ({ complete: true, ... }) has no context and no warnings key.
(5)Create core/tools/context.mjs: no side effects, no import from workflow.mjs or dtech-aidlc.mjs (it may later import knowledge.mjs, onboard.mjs and artifacts.mjs, which in turn never import workflow.mjs or context.mjs). It exports buildDirectiveContext(input), which returns null, and ARTIFACT_VALIDATORS = {} (called from ENG-09 on). A comment at the top states the contract: buildDirectiveContext is synchronous, is called once per 'orchestrate next' that selects a stage, before any write; input is { root, graph, config, state, stage, intentDir, isNewIntent, expectedArtifacts, artifactPathFor } (root is the absolute project root; graph the validated graph; config the validated .aidlc/config.json object or {}; state the intent's state object, read only, for a new intent the state that is about to be saved; stage the graph entry of the selected stage plus phaseGate; expectedArtifacts is [] and artifactPathFor returns null until ENG-09); the return value must be JSON-serialisable and is placed verbatim under the directive's top-level 'context' key; throwing an Error aborts 'orchestrate next' with that message and no file is created or changed. ARTIFACT_VALIDATORS maps an output id to (absolutePath, text, info) => array of problem strings, with info = { root, graph, state, stage, intentId, output, notApplicable }. ENG-09 adds the third export, extraRequiredArtifacts. From then on KNW and BRN own the bodies in this file; ENG owns the call sites.

Acceptance criteria

  • In a solo intent the directive for problem-framing has stage.phaseGate false, gate.id 'analysis-baseline', gate.finalStage 'context-and-risk' and approvalRequiredAfter 'context-and-risk'; the directive for context-and-risk has stage.phaseGate true.
  • In a team intent the directive for build-and-verify has gate.id 'release-candidate' and stage.phaseGate true, and the directive for red-tests has stage.phaseGate false.
  • A stage directive always has a top-level 'warnings' array, has no key named 'notices', and has no 'context' key while core/tools/context.mjs returns null; the object printed for a finished intent has neither 'warnings' nor 'context'.
  • 'node --test tests/directive.test.mjs' passes, including a test that calls orchestrateNext for a new intent with a contextProvider that throws Error('boom'), asserts that the call throws 'boom', and asserts that afterwards no folder exists under .aidlc/intents, no pointer file exists and audit.jsonl is byte-identical to before; and the same for an existing intent (intent state file byte-identical).
  • The same test file includes a test in which a contextProvider returning { a: 1 } produces a directive whose context deep-equals { a: 1 }, and in which the provider received an input object with exactly the keys root, graph, config, state, stage, intentDir, isNewIntent, expectedArtifacts and artifactPathFor.
  • grep -n "from './workflow.mjs'" core/tools/context.mjs prints nothing, and grep -c 'KNW-05\|HRN-24' core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs prints at least 3 (the marked dispatch positions exist).

Tests

  • tests/directive.test.mjs (new): CLI tests for the gate fields on a non-gate and a gate stage in solo and team scope and for the presence of 'warnings'; unit tests importing orchestrateNext from core/tools/workflow.mjs for the throwing provider (nothing written, new and existing intent), the returning provider (context attached, input keys) and the null provider (no context key). Projects are prepared with initProject.
  • Existing tests keep passing unchanged: tests/phase-graph-validation.test.mjs:29-34 and tests/agent-model-config.test.mjs:65-68 (phaseFile, agentFile, model, modelSource).

Risks

A conductor that read approvalRequiredAfter literally now sees the phase's final stage instead of the current stage; neither projected SKILL.md mentions the field, and the new value is what its name says. KNW-05, KNW-06, KNW-09, HRN-09 and HRN-24 start from this task's contract and must not edit the old line numbers dtech-aidlc.mjs:22-49 and :134-159, which no longer exist after milestone 1. If a workstream needs a further input field, it is added to the hook's input object here, not by changing the call order. A failure in a dispatch block that runs after orchestrateNext leaves state advanced and nothing printed; running the command again returns the same stage.

ENG-06New intents require an initialized project; a per-intent scope override is explicit and recordedP1S

Engine integrity · milestone 1 · effort S (under half a day)

Problem today

'orchestrate next --intent' works in a directory with no .aidlc/config.json and creates .aidlc there, including in a subdirectory of an initialized project, which silently forks state (reproduced by the review from a src/ subdirectory). The scope is taken from --scope before the configuration (core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:133), so after 'init --scope solo' the command 'orchestrate next --scope enterprise --intent ...' creates an enterprise intent while config.json says solo and doctor reports ok.

Depends on

  • ENG-05

Files

  • core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:35 (scope-change refusal), :38-47 (intent creation and its audit row), :133 (scope resolution); the same logic in core/tools/workflow.mjs (orchestrateNext) after ENG-05
  • tests/cli-integration.test.mjs:102, :131, :159
  • tests/phase-graph-validation.test.mjs:29
  • tests/intent-lifecycle.test.mjs

Change

(1)Creating a new intent requires that .aidlc/config.json exists. When it is absent, exit 1 before creating anything, with Project is not initialized at <root>. Run 'dtech-aidlc onboard --harness <claude|deepseek> --scope <solo|team|enterprise>' there first.; when a parent directory of <root> contains .aidlc/config.json, append An initialized project exists at <parent>; run the command there or pass --project <parent>. (walk up to the file-system root and name the nearest one; this is only a hint, the project root is still the current directory or --project). The command names --harness because a first init or onboard without it fails once HRN-06 is merged.
(2)Continuing an intent that already exists in a project without config.json (possible for projects started with the current version, such as this repository's own .aidlc) keeps working, and the directive's top-level 'warnings' array gets exactly one sentence: Project has an active intent but no .aidlc/config.json. Run dtech-aidlc onboard --harness <claude|deepseek> --scope <the intent's scope> to complete setup., where the intent's scope is substituted (for example '--scope solo') and '<claude|deepseek>' is printed literally. The command is written without quotation marks around it, exactly as in the doctor warning of ENG-10, so that the phrase 'Run dtech-aidlc onboard --harness <claude|deepseek> --scope solo' appears as one unbroken string.
(3)Scope of a new intent: --scope when given, else the scope in config.json (the default scope for new intents), validated with the existing validateScope ('scope must be solo, team, or enterprise', which also covers a config.json without a valid scope). Store scopeSource in the intent state: 'flag' whenever --scope was given for the new intent (also when its value equals the configured scope), otherwise 'config'. Print scope and scopeSource in the directive. When --scope differs from the configured scope, add the warning Intent scope '<x>' overrides the project scope '<y>' from .aidlc/config.json (given by --scope).; when it equals the configured scope no warning is added. The intent.created audit row becomes { intent, intentId, scope, scopeSource, projectScope }.
(4)For an intent that already exists, the scope is the intent's own and never changes; --scope equal to it is accepted and a different value is refused, as today, with the clearer text Intent '<id>' uses scope <x>; the scope cannot change after an intent starts. Omit --scope to continue it. The directive prints the stored scopeSource, or 'config' for intents created before this task.

Acceptance criteria

  • In an empty directory, 'orchestrate next --intent x' exits 1, stderr contains 'Project is not initialized' and 'dtech-aidlc onboard --harness', and no .aidlc directory exists afterwards.
  • From the src/ subdirectory of an initialized project, 'orchestrate next --intent x' exits 1, stderr contains the parent directory path and '--project', and src/.aidlc does not exist.
  • On the legacy fixture of ENG-02 (state file, no config.json), 'orchestrate next' exits 0 with intentId 'test' and the directive's warnings contain exactly one entry, which contains the unbroken string 'Run dtech-aidlc onboard --harness <claude|deepseek> --scope solo'.
  • After 'init --harness claude --scope solo', 'orchestrate next --scope enterprise --intent big' exits 0 with scope 'enterprise', scopeSource 'flag' and a warning containing 'overrides the project scope'; the intent.created audit row has scope 'enterprise', projectScope 'solo', scopeSource 'flag'.
  • After 'init --harness claude --scope team', 'orchestrate next --intent y' prints scope 'team' and scopeSource 'config' with an empty warnings array.
  • After 'init --harness claude --scope solo', 'orchestrate next --scope solo --intent z' prints scopeSource 'flag' with an empty warnings array.
  • For a running solo intent, 'orchestrate next --scope team' exits 1 with 'the scope cannot change after an intent starts', and 'orchestrate next --scope solo' exits 0.

  • Existing tests that break because they start an intent without init: tests/cli-integration.test.mjs:102 ('workflow keeps the original intent, ...'), :131 ('phase-final completion requires explicit approval; ...') and :159 ('dependency commands validate identifiers, ...'). Add a call cliJson(project, 'init', '--harness', 'claude', '--scope', 'solo') before the first 'orchestrate next' in each of the three tests; the '--scope solo' they pass then equals the project scope, so no warning appears.

The per-intent scope override stays possible by design (it is part of the shared rules for .aidlc/config.json); the warning makes it visible. HRN-24 pushes its own sentences into the same warnings array from main(); that needs no ENG change, and its tests assert 'no entry mentions harness refresh' instead of 'the array is empty' because of step (2). The helper init() at tests/agent-model-config.test.mjs:14 runs a bare 'init' with no --harness; it keeps working through milestone 2 and must be changed by HRN-06, which is the task that makes a bare first init fail.

ENG-07Truthful report records: keep --detail, write it to the audit log, return a blocked stage to in_progress, and never print or record an approval that was not givenP0M

Engine integrity · milestone 1 · effort M (up to two days)

Problem today

'orchestrate report' overwrites the stage row's detail on every report (core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs:156) and never writes it to the audit row (:158), so rejection feedback and skip reasons are lost. It prints approval 'approved' for every report on a gate stage, including blocked and skipped ones (:159), and writes gateApproval 'approved' to the audit log when '--result blocked --approval approved' is given (:158). 'skipped' and 'blocked' are accepted with no --detail. A blocked stage that 'orchestrate next' selects again keeps status 'blocked' because of the '??=' at :139. An unknown --stage value produces the misleading message 'No current stage; run orchestrate next first' (:149). The printed result names no intent (:159), so main() cannot name the knowledge record of the reported intent (KNW-06) without reading state itself.

  • tests/report-records.test.mjs (new)

(7)approval required at this gate), and write nothing on failure. Keep today's messages 'No active workflow state', 'No current stage; run orchestrate next first', Only the current stage (<id>) can be reported, '--result must be complete, blocked, or skipped' and Stage <id> is not included in the active <scope> scope. (2) --stage: when the value is not a stage id in the graph, fail with Unknown stage '<value>'. (3) --detail: required for '--result blocked' and '--result skipped' (--result <value> requires --detail "<reason>"); optional for complete. (4) --approval in this task: the only accepted value is 'approved' (--approval must be approved); together with '--result blocked' it is an error (--approval approved cannot be combined with --result blocked; a blocked report never passes a gate). The recorded approval value is 'approved' only when the stage is a gate stage, the result is complete or skipped, and --approval approved was given; in every other case it is null. (7) Output becomes { recorded: true, intentId, stage, result, phaseGate, gate, approval, intentComplete }, where intentId is the id of the intent the report was recorded on (main() uses it at the KNW-06 position to name the knowledge record, so no other module has to read state to learn it), approval is the recorded approval value, and intentComplete is true when deriveStatus is 'complete' after this report. Whenever the selected stage's most recent report is a blocked one (the last entry of 'reports' has result 'blocked', or, for a row written by an older version, the row had status 'blocked' and no 'reports' array), add to the directive stage.rework = { blockedAt: <the 'at' of that report, or the row's reportedAt>, detail: <its detail or null>, attempt: <number of entries in 'reports', or 1 when there is none, plus 1> }; this holds for repeated 'orchestrate next' calls until the stage is reported again. Problem today

On a stage that is not a gate stage, any of --approval, --approved-by or --approval-note is an error: Stage <id> is not a phase gate; --approval, --approved-by and --approval-note are only accepted on <final stage id>, the last stage of the <phase id> phase. --approved-by or --approval-note without --approval: --approved-by and --approval-note require --approval. --approval rejected with a result other than blocked: --approval rejected must be reported with --result blocked --detail "<the owner's feedback>". --approval approved with blocked: the ENG-07 error. --approved-by is trimmed and must be 1 to 200 characters without control characters (--approved-by must be 1 to 200 characters without control characters).

Risks

The approval is still a flag passed by whoever runs the CLI, which may be the AI conductor; this task makes it mandatory for every way of passing a gate and attributable, not unforgeable (see the open decision). A conductor that passes '--approval approved' on every stage (today's approvalRequiredAfter suggests every stage is a gate) is now refused on non-gate stages with a message naming the gate stage. Change

(1)Restructure doctor into a constant list DOCTOR_CHECKS in dtech-aidlc.mjs of functions (ctx) => array of { status, message }, where ctx is { root, graph (null when the graph failed to load), config } and status is 'pass', 'warn' or 'fail'. This task ships five functions: checkGraph (today's graph row and the 'Stage <id> references unknown agent' rows), checkConfig ('Project configuration and agent models'), checkDependencies ('Dependency repositories: <n> registered'), checkWorkflowState (new) and checkAudit ('Audit log contains valid JSON lines'), with the same messages as today for the existing ones. A check function that throws is reported as one 'fail' row with the error message. A comment above the list documents the final order for all workstreams: graph; configuration and agent models; projection (HRN-04); dependency repositories; knowledge (KNW-06, row starting 'Knowledge:'); knowledge sources (BRN-05, row starting 'Knowledge sources:'); workflow state (ENG-10); audit log; unused methodology copy (HRN-05). Each of those tasks adds exactly one function at its place in the list and changes nothing else in the doctor branch. The output is { ok, warnings, checks } from this task on: ok is false only when a row has status 'fail'; warnings is the number of rows with status 'warn'; the exit code is 1 only when ok is false. Severity rule for every check: a condition that stops the workflow or shows damaged data is 'fail'; a condition the user should act on while the workflow keeps running is 'warn'.
(2)checkWorkflowState(root, graph) in workflow.mjs, read-only, returning no rows when the graph is null; the list entry is ctx => checkWorkflowState(ctx.root, ctx.graph). Pointer: fail State pointer: .aidlc/state.json cannot be parsed or State pointer: .aidlc/state.json is not a recognised state file; fail State pointer: active intent '<id>' has no state file; warn State: version 1 format; it is migrated automatically by the next orchestrate or intent command (and then validate that old state as one intent); when workflow state exists (a pointer, an old-format root or at least one intent folder) and .aidlc/config.json is absent, warn Project has workflow state but no .aidlc/config.json; run dtech-aidlc onboard --harness <claude|deepseek> --scope <scope> (the two placeholders are printed literally, because intents can have different scopes). For every directory under .aidlc/intents whose name matches the id pattern: fail with Intent <id>: <problem> for each problem that validateIntentState (ENG-02) reports (all problems, not only the first; an unparseable file is one problem); and, when the state is valid: fail Intent <id>: stage <x> is not part of scope <scope> for a stage row of a graph stage outside the intent's scope; warn Intent <id>: stage <x> is not in the current graph for an unknown stage key; fail Intent <id>: stage <b> is recorded <status> although the earlier stage <a> is not finished when a complete or skipped stage follows, in scope order, a stage that is neither; fail Intent <id>: currentStage <x> is not the first unfinished stage when currentStage is set and differs from it; for every phase-final stage with status complete or skipped, with the gate id read from the graph by gateInfo: fail Intent <id>: gate <gate id> was passed without a recorded approval when the stage row has a 'reports' array and state.gates?.[<gate id>]?.decision is not 'approved', and warn Intent <id>: gate <gate id> was passed before approvals were recorded when the row has no 'reports' array (written by an older version); warn Intent <id>: artifact missing: <path> for each recorded artifact of a completed stage that no longer exists. Finish with one pass row Intents: <n> checked (<a> active, <p> paused, <c> complete, <x> abandoned), counted from listIntents (ENG-03). Every warn or fail row of this function therefore starts with 'State pointer:', 'State:', 'Project has workflow state' or 'Intent <id>:'; tests identify the function's rows by these prefixes.
(3)Close release 0.1.3. Set "version" in package.json to "0.1.3" (milestone 1 is release 0.1.3 and changes no file under harness/). Complete the section '## 0.1.3' of CHANGELOG.md, which ENG-01 created, with one entry per behaviour change of milestone 1: strict options (ENG-01, already there); state version 2, the automatic migration with the backup .aidlc/state.v1.bak.json, and the way back for the old CLI (copy the backup over .aidlc/state.json) (ENG-02); several intents per project and the commands intent list, pause, resume and abandon (ENG-03); 'orchestrate next --intent' fails in a project that was never initialized (ENG-06); blocked and skipped reports require --detail (ENG-07); a gate cannot be passed by completing or skipping without --approval approved, and --approved-by, --approval-note and --approval rejected exist (ENG-08); a stage cannot be reported complete until every file listed under artifacts.expected exists, one file per output (ENG-09); doctor prints { ok, warnings, checks } and checks state against the graph (this task); the entries that HRN-08 names and, if it was accepted, the gate rename of HRN-25.

Acceptance criteria

  • A pointer naming an intent whose folder was deleted makes 'doctor' exit 1 with 'has no state file'.

  • The legacy fixture of ENG-02 gives a warn containing 'version 1 format' and a warn containing 'run dtech-aidlc onboard --harness <claude|deepseek> --scope <scope>', exit code 0, and no file changes.
  • A freshly initialized project ('init --harness claude --scope solo'), and a project with one fully completed intent, give exit code 0 and an object whose keys are exactly ok, warnings and checks, with ok true, 'warnings' equal to the number of rows whose status is 'warn', and no warn or fail row whose message starts with 'State pointer:', 'State:', 'Project has workflow state' or 'Intent ' (the rows of checkWorkflowState). At the end of milestone 1 the printed 'warnings' value is 0 for both projects; the automated test does not assert the value 0, because HRN-04 later adds warn rows that depend on the machine, for example when dtech-aidlc is not on PATH.
  • grep -n 'DOCTOR_CHECKS' core/tools/dtech-aidlc.mjs shows the list, and the comment above it names, in order, graph, configuration, projection, dependency repositories, knowledge, knowledge sources, workflow state, audit log and unused methodology copy.
  • 'dtech-aidlc version' prints 'dtech-aidlc 0.1.3'; the section '## 0.1.3' of CHANGELOG.md mentions state.v1.bak.json, 'not initialized', '--approved-by' and 'artifacts.expected'.

Tests

  • tests/doctor-state.test.mjs (new): one test per acceptance line 1 to 7; fixtures are produced by running the CLI (initProject, driveToCompletion) and then editing the per-intent state.json in the test. Assertions about a healthy project check 'ok', the key set, that 'warnings' equals the count of warn rows, and the absence of warn or fail rows with the prefixes of checkWorkflowState; they never assert that 'warnings' is 0 or that the list has a fixed length, so that the functions other workstreams add to DOCTOR_CHECKS do not break this file.

Risks

Projects whose state was hand-edited or produced by the gate bypass of the old version may now show warnings; rows written by the old version are downgraded to warnings by the 'reports' test, so only state written after ENG-07 can fail the gate check. The gate check looks approvals up by the gate id that the graph gives today; a gate renamed after ENG-08 has shipped would turn every earlier approval into a failure, which is why HRN-25 is done before ENG-08 or not at all. HRN-04, HRN-05, KNW-06 and BRN-05 add functions to DOCTOR_CHECKS; the list and the output shape { ok, warnings, checks } are the only shared surface and neither changes again. If the owner cuts releases in a separate commit, the version change of step (3) moves to that commit.

Change

New module core/tools/projection.mjs. It imports only lib.mjs and Node built-ins, never workflow.mjs or context.mjs. Exports: hashText(buffer): SHA-256 hex (node:crypto) of the content after replacing every CRLF with LF. stampPath(root, manifest): <root>/<skillDir>/.projection.json. readStamp(root, manifest): returns null when the file is absent, is a symbolic link, is not valid JSON or does not have schemaVersion 1. writeStamp(root, manifest, stamp): serialises the stamp and, when the text differs from what is on disk, writes it with writeFileAtomic(path, text, { mode: 0o644 }) from lib.mjs (ENG-02), which is atomic and refuses a symbolic-link target with 'Refusing to write through symlink: <path>'; it writes nothing when the text is unchanged; do not write a second atomic-write helper. projectionStatus(root, manifest, engineVersion): applies the file and harness state rules of design section 3 (without the history table and without obsolete files, both added by HRN-03) and returns {harness, invoke, skillDir, state, stampedEngineVersion, files:[{path,state}], obsolete:[]}. compareVersions(a, b): compares three integers; an unparsable value counts as 0.0.0. The stamp is {"schemaVersion":1,"harness":"<name>","engineVersion":"<x.y.z>" or null,"files":{"<target>":{"sha256":"<hex>"}}}, serialised with JSON.stringify(stamp, null, 2) plus a final newline, keys in that order, and contains no timestamp and no absolute path. In lib.mjs add configuredHarnesses(config): returns config.harnesses when it is a non-empty array whose entries are all in listHarnesses(), otherwise [config.harness] when that is in listHarnesses(), otherwise []. In init/onboard (step 9), after projecting each harness, update its stamp: start from the existing stamp, or from {schemaVersion:1, harness, engineVersion:null, files:{}}; for every shipped file whose on-disk hash equals the engine source hash, set that file's entry to the hash; leave other entries as they are; if every shipped file is current and the existing engineVersion is not greater than the running version, set engineVersion to the running version; never lower engineVersion. Add to the init/onboard output the key 'projections': [{harness, skillDir (absolute), state}]. New command 'dtech-aidlc harness status': read-only; prints {engineVersion, harnesses:[...], legacyMethodology:null} for the configured harnesses, and {engineVersion, harnesses:[], legacyMethodology:null} when the project has no valid config. Register it in core/tools/cli-spec.mjs as the row 'harness status' {} with 0 arguments (the two-word key list of ENG-01 already contains 'harness'); write no option check in the branch. A missing or unknown harness action throws 'Use harness status' (extended by HRN-03 and HRN-06). Add one entry to the HELP array, ' harness status Show the state of the projected skill files', and add 'harness:Inspect and refresh projected skill files' to the commands list of completion.zsh, with a case offering the action 'status'; tests/completion.test.mjs (HRN-08) fails if either is missing. Set package.json to version 0.2.0 (release rule: the first release that writes stamps).

  • 'dtech-aidlc harness status' prints state 'current'; after appending a line to SKILL.md it prints 'modified' for the harness and for SKILL.md; after deleting SKILL.md it prints 'missing'.

Output as in design section 4; needsAttention is true when any action is kept-modified, kept-modified-obsolete, refused-ahead or refused-not-a-regular-file.   • The 0.1.1 fixture with an edited legacy SKILL.md: the file remains, is reported 'kept-modified-obsolete', also with --force, and 'harness status' prints 'modified'.

  • A harness in state 'ahead' is not changed, the action is 'refused-ahead' and the command exits 1; with --force it is replaced and the command exits 0.

The test asserts no totals, because the totals depend on the end commit of the range.

Risks

Deleting files in a user's repository is the sensitive part: deletion is per file, only on an exact hash match, never recursive and never forced. A user who installed from an unmerged branch, or who still has the skill of the unrelated product that lived in this repository before commit 91c9eea, has files whose hashes are not in the table; they are reported as modified and kept, which is safe. The table has a timing constraint: a methodology copy made from a commit that is not in the range is reported as edited and never removed, which is why HRN-05 must merge directly after this task and the table must be regenerated if anything under core/methodology changes in between. The 'ahead' protection relies on version bumps (release rule in the design).
